report.summary: (model supplied no summary; its answer is preserved in handoff)

handoff.purpose: Implements session event streaming, line/typed-event parsing, and process lifecycle control (approve/reject/interrupt/terminate) for CLI subprocess adapters.

symbols.name: _parse_line
symbols.note: Parses a single output line into an AgentEvent; falls back to TextDelta on JSON parse failure or non-dict JSON.

symbols.name: _parse_typed_event
symbols.note: Maps a typed event dict to a specific AgentEvent subtype; unknown event types become AgentMessage with role='system'.

symbols.name: approve
symbols.note: Raises NotImplementedError; no approval protocol implemented.

symbols.name: reject
symbols.note: Raises NotImplementedError; no approval protocol implemented.

symbols.name: interrupt
symbols.note: Sends SIGINT to the session process if it is still running; ignores ProcessLookupError/OSError.

symbols.name: _stop_process
symbols.note: Terminates a process, then kills after 5s timeout; ignores ProcessLookupError/OSError.

symbols.name: terminate
symbols.note: Stops the session process and awaits/cancels the stderr task; removes session and sequence mappings.

claims.text: Lifecycle events are still observable, but aren't misrepresented as text generated by the model.
claims.why: The fallback for unknown event types returns AgentMessage(content=json.dumps(data), role='system'), which is an AgentMessage, not a lifecycle-specific event type; the comment claims lifecycle events are observable, but the code returns a generic AgentMessage with role='system' — arguably still misrepresenting them as model messages with a role.

claims.text: one-shot CLI profiles do not expose a portable approval protocol
claims.why: Both methods unconditionally raise NotImplementedError with the given message; no alternative path exists in this chunk.
The code checks session is None or process.stdout is None and raises RuntimeError with that message.
Both branches raise TimeoutError with the exact message; one when remaining <= 0, one on asyncio.TimeoutError.
The code awaits session.stderr_task after process.wait() and decodes it; the task is expected to capture stderr.

observations.what: The parser's fallback for unknown event types returns AgentMessage with role='system', which may not be a distinct lifecycle event type; the comment claims it is not misrepresented as model text.
In _parse_typed_event, for 'assistant' event with content list, if text is empty it returns TextDelta(json.dumps(data)) — this may duplicate the fallback behavior.

The timeout check computes remaining = timeout_s - (monotonic - started_at) and then uses it as the timeout for asyncio.wait_for; if remaining is a float, asyncio.wait_for accepts it, but the check for <=0 is fine.
The parser for 'result' event returns AgentMessage(content=...) where content may be a dict (usage) converted to JSON string; this may not be a text message.
The parser for 'tool_result' uses data.get('content') or data.get('result') — if content is an empty list, it falls back to result; if both are falsy, result is None, which may be unexpected.

risks: _parse_typed_event fallback | medium | Lifecycle events are returned as AgentMessage with role='system', which may still be interpreted as model output by consumers; the comment claims they are not misrepresented.
assistant branch | low | If content list has no text blocks, returns TextDelta(json.dumps(data)) instead of a more structured event; may be confusing.
result branch | low | Usage dict is stringified into AgentMessage content, which may not be a text message.
tool_result branch | low | If content is an empty list and result is absent, ToolCompleted.result is None; may be surprising.
